notes.scope: SQL Server 2022 schema buckets and exploration hints for the existing 130-node rules. This file does not add graph nodes, change candidate compatibility, or enable a database executor.
notes.abstract_types: The active COL_INT/VALUE_TYPICAL_INT, COL_FLOAT/VALUE_TYPICAL_FLOAT and COL_STRING/VALUE_TYPICAL_STRING terminals retain INT, FLOAT and STRING; core rules map them to T_CMP, T_CMP and T_STR. BIT is an int-bucket scalar, not T_BOOL.
notes.unicode_function_collision: NCHAR column types are recognized by the existing substring match for char. Do not add the exact keyword nchar: predicate abstraction also treats mapping keywords as removable wrappers and would erase the supported NCHAR() function.
notes.bucket_order: Keep binary before date: timestamp contains time but denotes binary row-version data in SQL Server. BINARY, VARBINARY, IMAGE, ROWVERSION and TIMESTAMP are never character or temporal buckets.
notes.schema_only_buckets: date, binary and uniqueidentifier classify physical columns without adding COL_DATE, COL_BINARY or COL_UNIQUEIDENTIFIER to the candidate universe. Their generated DSL wrappers are not part of the current 130-node scope.
notes.legacy_lob_types: TEXT/NTEXT remain character storage and IMAGE remains binary storage. Bucket membership does not imply support for every comparison or function; concrete operand legality still requires SQL Server validation.
notes.json_storage: SQL Server 2022 stores JSON text in character columns such as NVARCHAR(MAX); it has no native JSON column type. Such columns share the string bucket used by ISJSON(). XML is kept separate.
notes.unsupported_types: XML, GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY, HIERARCHYID and SQL_VARIANT are segregated in unsupported; the current core rules provide no terminal or wrapper for that bucket. This is not a runtime exclusion filter: the unchanged heuristic still uses all columns when a requested bucket is empty, and unknown types can still fall back to string.
notes.operator_partition: The seven common arithmetic/comparison operators are baseline frequency hints, not measured SQL Server statistics. The remaining 97 definitions are exploration targets. Terminals, subqueries, volatile functions, CHAR(), COMPRESS() and DECOMPRESS() are not exploration targets.
notes.cleaning: The active candidate-bitmap path obtains its operator universe from sqlserver_rules.json. No extra text/prefix blacklist is needed here; the legacy generated-token cleaner is outside this task's scope.
notes.loader_boundary: Existing datatype readers also iterate the operator_profile metadata as a bucket; this file follows the established format and does not use that metadata bucket as a graph type. SQL Server identifier quoting, row limits, unknown/empty-bucket fallback and unsupported-wrapper rejection require later code adaptation.
